answer_1.quote: In this paper, we evaluate the suitability of large language models to support the editorial process of customer help pages... The reformulation task involves transforming a text that may contain potential orthographic errors, complicated or unclear structure... into a text containing the most relevant information written in a stylistically clear way understandable for a broad range of customers.
datasets: FAQ question‑answer pairs dataset provided by Deutsche Telekom AG
answer_1.outputs: Rewritten FAQ question‑answer pairs (up to three reformulation suggestions per input)

answer_2.quote: We analyzed the generated texts using ROUGE, a traditional n‑gram‑based text similarity metric, and BERTScore, a metric relying on dense vector embeddings to approximate the semantic similarity between generated text and the groundtruth.

answer_3.quote: We followed the work of ... and utilized GPT‑4 to score the output texts on a Likert scale of 1‑5 stars using the evaluation prompts listed in Table ... The highest rated Hallucination ... Coherence ... The model for all three criteria is GPT‑4 itself.
methods: LLM‑based Likert scoring via GPT‑4 prompts

answer_4.quote: Seven editors of different professional experience levels were tasked with evaluating those 120 pairs... Each editor assessed a random set of 30 pairs... The editors were prompted to address the following three questions: 1. Which reformulation of the input is superior... 2. On a scale, how much revision would be necessary for the better of the two suggestions... 3. Would the superior suggestion aid your work (e.g., save time)?
answer_4.guideline: Editors answered three questions: preference between two reformulations, amount of revision needed (scale from entirely to not at all), and whether the suggestion would help their work.
